details.performed: a person looked at the simulation in P14 and answered item 1 of the mast checklist (since deleted); no item of the current checklist (1 to 8) has a recorded answer

answered_before_the_lift.1: (item 1 as it stood in P14, about the mast) the mast read as a thin spike. Its dimensions were those of an HFS6-60120 profile 14 mm shorter than the 1250 mm Alex specified on 28 Sep, so the appearance was an accurate thin extrusion and not a sizing defect; its orientation and its mass were defects (V01-F1, V01-F2), both now closed. The mast is gone: item 1 of the checklist now asks about the lift column and has no recorded answer

findings.found: the mast profile was probably rotated 90 degrees: mast_section [0.060, 0.120] put 60 mm fore-aft and 120 mm lateral; option B (P-03 rev18.9 item 18) orients the same HFS6-60120 cross-section (its 340 mm arm profile, not a full-height mast) 120 mm fore-aft and 60 mm lateral, the stiff direction against the arms' forward cantilever. The value was right. Its axis assignment was only a prose note in the datum ('orientation unconfirmed') and no test asserted it
findings.outcome: confirmed correct by the design owner (Alex, 12 Oct 2026: 'thanks for catching the profile orientation, that's exactly the kind of check we need'); the 90 degree rotation was real
findings.resolved_by: the mast and mast_section are deleted (P15); the rule it proposed is implemented: a dimension list declares axis_convention and T12 asserts the assignment against the expansion

findings.found: mast_mass was 3.0 kg (placeholder) for 1.2365 m of HFS6-60120: about 337 kg/m3 over the bounding box, low by roughly 2.5 to 4 times for an aluminium extrusion (an estimate, not a datasheet figure). Labelled placeholder, so nothing lied, but the placeholder was implausible and nothing checked plausibility
findings.outcome: closed by the supplier catalogue figure: the lift is a DOLD Hexalift V4 350 of 11.7 kg (rev19.0, 12 Oct 2026). The estimate was 7.5 to 12 kg; the catalogue value is at the top of that bracket
findings.resolved_by: mast_mass is deleted with the mast; lift_mass_dold_v4_350 carries 11.7 kg (provisional: a catalogue figure, not weighed); the rule it proposed is implemented: a mass datum of ours declares a density_band and T10 checks it

details.reading: The manual check found what the automated ones could not: no test of ours examined an axis assignment or the plausibility of a placeholder, and the two rules it proposed are now checks (T12, T10). V01 stays WARN: no item of the current checklist (items 2 to 8 and the rewritten item 1) has a recorded answer, and a closed finding is not an answered checklist

limitations: placeholder datums: 4 of 13 (left_wrist_camera_pose, lift_column_section, lift_mass_tl3_400, right_wrist_camera_pose)

base inertials are platform-sw CAD-export placeholders, the lift mass is a catalogue figure (11.7 kg, provisional) on a placeholder box, and the arm masses are upstream nominal values; none of them is a measured mass

T05 asserts the shoulder height at every lift stop (height(openarm_{left,right}_base_link) above the floor = lift_calibration_stops[stop]) and the three stops are calibration IDs, not inputs of the configuration id; it does not validate the datums themselves

E01 is WARN, never PASS: height, width and depth are lower bounds from zero pose, link frame origins and box/cylinder/sphere extents; mesh extents are not included, so a figure under the limit proves nothing about the real envelope. A4 decides

T10 reports what the description models. The battery, hub motors, electronics and the lift column's structure beyond its catalogue mass are not modelled, so the total is not the gross mass of the robot

the lift column has no collision geometry: its lateral extent is not sourced, so the arms can plan through the column body; the arm profile (option B's 340 mm box) is the only collision body of the upper structure

T14, T15 and T16 are expansion checks: nothing here loads the gazebo or the real plugin (the gazebo profile report, G01 and G02, is where the gazebo one runs), and the real profile cannot even be built here (openarm_hardware needs OpenArmCAN)

the gripper controllers are the deprecated position_controllers/GripperActionController on purpose: the replacement serves ParallelGripperCommand instead of GripperCommand, which would decide manipulation#11 / ADR-009 point 4 (open)
L01 launches mock.launch.py only: controller_manager on mock_components/GenericSystem, which reflects its command back as state, so it shows the controller wiring and not tracking performance
T02 check_urdf parses the XML and builds the link tree; it does not resolve package:// mesh URIs

W01: KDL consumers (robot_state_publisher, MoveIt in A7) drop the inertia of the root link; the root is base_footprint since platform-sw 935efc7 and carries none, so base_link's 4.18 kg is no longer the one dropped

W02: with enable_planar_base:=true KDL consumers see world -> base_footprint as static; planar base motion can never come from robot_state_publisher (A7: it comes from Gazebo's odom -> base_footprint, ADR-003 / ADR-005 / REP 105)

V01 is WARN: P14's manual look at the mast found two defects (V01-F1 confirmed correct by the design owner, V01-F2 closed by the 11.7 kg catalogue figure) and both are resolved by the lift; the current checklist, which states what to measure, has no recorded answer. This report launches nothing for V01 and records no inspection of its own
config ids are hashes of xacro's output text: a different xacro version that formats a number differently gives a different id for the same sources

`static+mock` names the evidence class: expansions of every hardware_profile, plus a headless launch of the mock bringup (L01) and the robot_state_publisher observation for W02. Nothing in this report ran on Gazebo or real hardware
no physical evidence; static expansion and zero-pose FK only
